flags.explanation: The source refers only to “any of the components”; “al principio activo” is an unsupported addition and may suggest a separate active-ingredient allergy criterion.
flags.span: al principio activo o a cualquiera de los demás componentes

flags.explanation: “Vacuna” is feminine in Spanish; the phrase should be “puede ser administrada”. Alternatively, the standard leaflet formulation is “puede administrarse”.
flags.span: puede ser administrado

flags.explanation: The source states the opposite: ZOSTAVAX should not be given to pregnant women. This reverses an important contraindication and could cause harm.
flags.span: ZOSTAVAX debe administrarse a mujeres embarazadas.

flags.explanation: This does not translate the source sentence about driving and using machines; it incorrectly repeats the heading for the following section on ingredients. The information that there is no evidence of an effect on driving or machine use is omitted.
flags.span: Información importante sobre algunos de los componentes de ZOSTAVAX

flags.explanation: “ZOSTAVAX” refers to a vaccine and is conventionally feminine in Spanish; the phrase should be “debe ser inyectada”. “Debe inyectarse” is also more natural.
flags.span: ZOSTAVAX debe ser inyectado

flags.explanation: “Bruising” is mistranslated as “ardor”, while “warmth” is rendered as “calor”. The target omits bruising and adds burning, changing the listed adverse effects. It should say “calor y hematomas/moretones”.
flags.span: calor y ardor

flags.explanation: The translation reverses the meaning of “should not be given” by stating that ZOSTAVAX should be administered to pregnant women.
flags.span: debe administrarse

flags.explanation: The section heading “Pregnancy and breast-feeding” is omitted from the translation.
flags.span: ZOSTAVAX debe administrarse a mujeres embarazadas.

flags.explanation: ZOSTAVAX se identifica como una vacuna femenina (“está indicada”), por lo que el participio debe concordar como “administrada”.
flags.span: ZOSTAVAX puede ser administrado al mismo tiempo que la vacuna antigripal inactivada.

flags.explanation: ZOSTAVAX se identifica como una vacuna femenina (“está indicada”), por lo que el participio debe concordar como “inyectada”.
flags.span: ZOSTAVAX debe ser inyectado bajo la piel (vía subcutánea), preferentemente en la parte superior del brazo.

flags.explanation: The bullet items begin with conditional clauses but lack the governing lead-in “No reciba ZOSTAVAX”, and the parenthetical continuation is also interrupted by “Información adicional - qué contiene ZOSTAVAX” before its closing parenthesis.
flags.span: • si es alérgico (hipersensible) al principio activo o a cualquiera de los demás componentes (por ejemplo, neomicina) de ZOSTAVAX (incluyendo cualquiera de los componentes incluidos en “los demás componentes son” – ver sección 6. Información adicional - qué contiene ZOSTAVAX) • si tiene trastornos sanguíneos o cualquier tipo de cáncer que debilite su sistema inmune

flags.explanation: The parenthetical is grammatically disrupted because “Información adicional - qué contiene ZOSTAVAX” is inserted before the closing parenthesis and does not complete the preceding list reference.
flags.span: Informe a su médico si usted ha tenido alguna vez una reacción alérgica a cualquiera de los componentes (incluyendo neomicina o cualquier otro componente incluido en “ los demás componentes son” – ver sección 6. Información adicional - qué contiene ZOSTAVAX) antes de recibir esta vacuna.

flags.explanation: The translation omits the source's statement that there is no information suggesting an effect on the ability to drive or use machines and replaces it with an unrelated heading.
flags.span: Información importante sobre algunos de los componentes de ZOSTAVAX

flags.explanation: The translation omits that the rash is blistering and instead adds a burning sensation.
flags.span: El herpes zóster es una erupción dolorosa y con sensación de quemazón.

flags.explanation: The translation adds “the active ingredient,” which is not stated in the source.
flags.span: si es alérgico (hipersensible) al principio activo o a cualquiera de los demás componentes

flags.explanation: This translates the heading about important ingredient information rather than the source’s information about driving and using machines.
flags.span: Información importante sobre algunos de los componentes de ZOSTAVAX

flags.explanation: The translation says “any other ingredient” instead of preserving the source’s reference to any ingredients listed under “the other ingredients are,” thereby altering the scope of the allergy information.
flags.span: Informe a su médico si usted ha tenido alguna vez una reacción alérgica a cualquiera de los componentes (incluyendo neomicina o cualquier otro componente incluido en “ los demás componentes son” – ver sección 6. Información adicional - qué contiene ZOSTAVAX) antes de recibir esta vacuna.

flags.explanation: The translation omits bruising and adds burning, whereas the source lists warmth and bruising.
flags.span: Estos efectos adversos incluyeron enrojecimiento, dolor, hinchazón, prurito, calor y ardor en el lugar de inyección.

flags.explanation: The translation omits that the allergic reactions may be serious.
flags.span: reacciones alérgicas, que pueden incluir dificultad para respirar o tragar.

flags.explanation: Omits the important warning that the allergic reactions may be serious; it should state that they may be serious and may include difficulty breathing or swallowing.
flags.span: que pueden incluir dificultad para respirar o tragar

flags.explanation: “Have been reported” is translated as “have been observed,” which changes the reporting context slightly, although the general meaning is preserved.
flags.span: se han observado

flags.explanation: “Blistering” is omitted. The target describes a burning sensation instead, which is not stated in the source, and fails to convey that the rash consists of blisters.
flags.span: una erupción dolorosa y con sensación de quemazón

flags.explanation: The source refers to allergy to any of the components of ZOSTAVAX. Introducing “al principio activo” is inaccurate and changes the terminology, since neomycin and the listed ingredients are components/excipients rather than necessarily the active ingredient.
flags.span: al principio activo o a cualquiera de los demás componentes

flags.explanation: The Spanish text does not translate “Driving and using machines” or the statement that there is no information suggesting an effect on driving or operating machinery. Instead, it repeats the heading belonging to the following section, causing an important omission and a coherence error.
flags.span: Información importante sobre algunos de los componentes de ZOSTAVAX

flags.explanation: “Bruising” is omitted. “Ardor” is added, although it is not present in the source; the source lists warmth and bruising as separate injection-site effects.
flags.span: enrojecimiento, dolor, hinchazón, prurito, calor y ardor

flags.explanation: The important qualification “which may be serious” is omitted from the description of allergic reactions, weakening the warning about potentially serious adverse effects.
flags.span: reacciones alérgicas, que pueden incluir dificultad para respirar o tragar

flags.explanation: Omits that the allergic reactions may be serious, an important safety qualification in the source.
flags.span: que pueden incluir dificultad para respirar o tragar

flags.explanation: Translates “have been reported” as “have been observed”; the source refers to reported cases, not necessarily direct observation.
flags.span: se han observado

flags.explanation: The translation omits the prohibition “Do not receive ZOSTAVAX,” leaving only the allergic condition without stating what must not be done.
flags.span: • si es alérgico (hipersensible) al principio activo o a cualquiera de los demás componentes (por ejemplo, neomicina) de ZOSTAVAX (incluyendo cualquiera de los componentes incluidos en “los demás componentes son” – ver sección 6.

flags.explanation: The translation replaces the source’s negative statement that there is no information suggesting an effect on driving or operating machines, omitting that negation and condition entirely.
flags.span: Información importante sobre algunos de los componentes de ZOSTAVAX

flags.explanation: “Blistering rash” is mistranslated as a rash with a burning sensation, omitting the meaning that it is covered with blisters.
flags.span: El herpes zóster es una erupción dolorosa y con sensación de quemazón.

flags.explanation: This omits the source information that ZOSTAVAX does not affect the ability to drive or use machines and instead introduces an unrelated heading about ingredients.
flags.span: Información importante sobre algunos de los componentes de ZOSTAVAX

flags.explanation: “Bruising” is mistranslated as “ardor,” so bruising is omitted and burning is incorrectly added.
flags.span: Estos efectos adversos incluyeron enrojecimiento, dolor, hinchazón, prurito, calor y ardor en el lugar de inyección.

flags.explanation: This segment addresses the reader with the informal “tú” form, whereas the rest of the leaflet consistently uses the formal “usted” form.
flags.span: Informa a tu médico si estás en periodo de lactancia o vas a estarlo.

flags.explanation: The informal second-person form (“tu”) is inconsistent with the formal register used throughout the leaflet (e.g., “Informe a su médico”, “Su médico”). It should be “Informe a su médico”.
flags.span: Informa a tu médico

flags.explanation: “Blistering rash” means an eruption with blisters or ampoules ("erupción con ampollas"), not a burning sensation. The blistering characteristic is omitted and a different symptom is introduced.
flags.span: una erupción dolorosa y con sensación de quemazón

flags.explanation: The source refers to allergy to any of ZOSTAVAX’s components. “Al principio activo” adds a specific concept that is not present in the source and is potentially inaccurate for a vaccine formulation.
flags.span: al principio activo o a cualquiera de los demás componentes

flags.explanation: In a Spanish (Spain) medicinal product leaflet, the standard technical term is “sistema inmunitario”; “sistema inmune” is less appropriate terminology.
flags.span: sistema inmune

flags.explanation: Segment 21 is a heading in the source (“Take special care with ZOSTAVAX”), but the translation turns it into an instruction that duplicates the opening of segment 22. This disrupts the document’s heading/content structure.
flags.span: Consulte con su médico o farmacéutico antes de ser vacunado con ZOSTAVAX:

flags.explanation: The leaflet consistently uses formal address (“usted”/imperative forms such as “Informe” and “Consulte”), but this sentence switches to informal second-person singular (“tu”, “Informa”).
flags.span: Informa a tu médico si estás en periodo de lactancia o vas a estarlo.

flags.explanation: The source states that there is no information suggesting that ZOSTAVAX affects the ability to drive or use machines. The Spanish text instead translates the heading from segment 35, omitting the entire driving-and-machines information and creating a misplaced heading.
flags.span: Información importante sobre algunos de los componentes de ZOSTAVAX

flags.explanation: The source says “any of the ingredients listed”; “cualquier otro componente” adds “other”, which changes the scope slightly and is inconsistent with the intended reference to all listed ingredients.
flags.span: cualquier otro componente incluido

flags.explanation: “Warmth” is correctly rendered by “calor”, but “bruising” is mistranslated as “ardor”. Bruising should be “hematomas”, “moratones” or similar. The translation therefore omits bruising and adds burning.
flags.span: calor y ardor

flags.explanation: The Spain leaflet otherwise uses “herpes zóster” or “zóster”. “Culebrilla” is not the preferred Spanish (Spain) medical term and creates terminology inconsistency within the document.
flags.span: culebrilla
